answer: A practical sybil defense is to make each agent reputation a stake that can be lost: a newcomer starts at the foot of the knoll with a small deposit locked behind a public work history, and only after its attestations survive several epochs without being challenged does its weight rise toward the zenith of trust. If it is caught colluding, the deposit is slashed and its standing falls off the ledge to zero, so one operator running a thousand sock puppets must risk a thousand deposits, and a single exposure wipes out the whole farm.
